Option1Stmt.S: $x + \log(e^x + 1) - 2 \log(2e^x + 1) + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration

Option2Stmt.S: $x - \log(e^x + 1) + 4 \log(e^x + 1) + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration

Option3Stmt.S: $x + \log(e^x + 1) - 4 \log(2e^x + 1) + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration

Option4Stmt.S: $x - \log(e^x + 1) + 2 \log(2e^x + 1) + c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration

Solution.S:
Let $I = \int \frac{dx}{2e^{2x} + 3e^x + 1}$

Let $e^x = t \Rightarrow e^x dx = dt \Rightarrow dx = \frac{dt}{t}$

$$I = \int \frac{dt}{t(2t^2 + 3t + 1)} = \int \frac{dt}{t(2t+1)(t+1)}$$

Let
$$\frac{1}{t(2t+1)(t+1)} = \frac{A}{t} + \frac{B}{2t+1} + \frac{C}{t+1}$$
$$\Rightarrow 1 = A(2t+1)(t+1) + Bt(t+1) + Ct(2t+1) \quad \text{(i)}$$

Put $t = -1$ in (i): $C = 1$
Put $t = -\frac{1}{2}$ in (i): $B = -4$
Put $t = 0$ in (i): $A = 1$

$$\therefore I = \int \frac{1}{t} dt - 4 \int \frac{1}{2t+1} dt + \int \frac{1}{t+1} dt$$
$$= \log t - \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \log|2t+1| + \log|t+1| + c$$
$$= \log e^x + \log(e^x+1) - 2\log(2e^x+1) + c$$
$$= x + \log(e^x+1) - 2\log(2e^x+1) + c$$

Thus the correct option is A.
